45: ## Shared semantic dictionary and component matrix
57: | Component | Source | Lean/native comparison |
58: |---|---|---|
59: | Ambient domain | Countable X, implicitly nondegenerate in examples | Selected uniform/limit existence targets explicitly require `Nonempty` and `Countable`; other general lemmas drop these. Nonempty is a real specialization for empty-X/empty-H edge cases. |
60: | Groups | Countable covering collection; Section 3 partition | Nat-indexed sets. Partition is exactly disjointness plus union=univ, allowing empty pieces. Fin k families extend by empty sets, preserving finite-partition mathematics. |
61: | Law/loss | Arbitrary discrete law; worst group error | Real summable normalized masses; ENNReal supremum of absolute coordinate errors. For positive a, the inequality is equivalent to all coordinate bounds. Supremum avoids the source's potentially unattained countable “max.” |
62: | Time/freshness | Representation always; correctness eventually | Accuracy only at positive times; finite histories include time zero with an arbitrary default law. Later consistency includes its starting time. Empty/exhausted target cases are not silently supplied fresh points. |
63: | Closure | Bottom when version space empty | Option closure and a total common core. Bad witnesses separately require nonempty version space, preventing vacuous core from acting as source nonbottom closure. |
64: | Dimension | Two strict badness inequalities | Both alternatives retained. The second includes a finite-live-index certificate; for a>0 infinite capacity cannot satisfy the strict inequality. “Finite dimension” is bounded bad cardinalities, with no least-value function. |
65: | Positive finite support | Sum over group-subcollection positive intersections | `HasFiniteSupport` uses all index subsets, including infinite ones, zero contribution for infinite intersections. For an injective indexing this is the literal source sum. Repeated identical groups can create index multiplicity absent from a set-of-groups reading. |
66: | Exact-profile support | Not Definition 4.1 | `HasFiniteExactProfileSupport` instead makes finite the union of points in finite exact membership cells. All positive and negative membership coordinates matter. It cannot be substituted without changing the theorem. |
67: | Computation | Semantic existence in Sections 3–4; finite oracle queries only in 4.9 | Semantic generators remain arbitrary functions. Query algorithms have finite adaptive transcripts, a computable controller in the selected impossibility, and a total arbitrary law decoder. No sampler is supplied or inferred. |
